issues.object: Overall room illumination and equipment exposure
issues.description: The room is uniformly subdued and grey despite the large bright ceiling panels. Equipment fronts, table padding and metal frames have little tonal separation, and the surgical area does not read as a well-illuminated clinical workspace.
issues.why: The luminous fixtures and the illumination they appear to produce are poorly balanced. Compared with the benchmark, the equipment lacks readable highlights and soft directional modelling.
issues.correct_result: Neutral hospital illumination with readable equipment surfaces, controlled luminous panels, soft shadows and sufficient indirect fill without washing out the room.
issues.root_cause: Panel emission may be primarily visual, with insufficient baked fixture contribution or indirect illumination; exposure may also be too low.
issues.proposed_fix: Check URP linear colour space and exposure first. Use baked neutral-white area-light contributions aligned to the ceiling panels, rebake indirect lighting, and supply light probes for movable equipment. Tune illumination before increasing panel emission; retain a neutral daylight white balance and avoid warm grading.
issues.expected: The workstation and table will become clearly readable while the room retains controlled highlights and a neutral clinical appearance.
issues.verification_needed: Repeat ot1_from_door and c1_table with unchanged camera framing, showing brighter equipment midtones without clipped fixture faces.

history.evidence: ot1_from_door shows bright ceiling panels above a uniformly subdued room; c1_table and c2_anaesthesia show dark padding and low tonal separation across equipment fronts and frames.
ot1_from_door and c1_table: equipment fronts, teal padding and exposed frames remain subdued despite bright ceiling panels.

issues.object: Floor beneath trolley casters, anaesthesia workstation, Mayo stand and operating-table base
issues.description: Floor contact and cast shadows are extremely weak beneath the equipment. Wheels and bases appear insufficiently anchored to the floor.
issues.why: Even under broad ceiling illumination, the narrow gaps beneath casters and equipment bases should produce localized occlusion and soft grounding shadows.
issues.correct_result: Soft, restrained cast shadows with clear dark contact immediately under wheels and bases.
issues.root_cause: Equipment may not be contributing to the bake, shadow reception may be disabled, or shadow bias and lightmap resolution may be losing small contacts.
issues.proposed_fix: Verify floor shadow reception, caster-to-floor contact and renderer shadow settings. Include static equipment in the lighting bake where appropriate, improve floor lightmap density around equipment, and reduce excessive shadow bias. For movable props, use a Quest-budgeted shadow solution rather than relying on ambient fill alone.
issues.expected: Equipment will sit convincingly on the floor instead of appearing visually detached.
issues.verification_needed: Provide a low-angle close-up of trolley and Mayo casters plus the original doorway view, with visible contact shadows and no detached shadow gaps.

history.evidence: c1_table, c2_anaesthesia and c4_cupboard_mayo show visible soft floor shadows beneath the trolley, workstation and Mayo stand. These are predominantly blurred patches, with limited correspondence to individual legs and frame members.
c1_table and c6_staff: shadows are visible beneath the trolley and Mayo stand, but wheel contact is inconsistent and broad dark patches dominate beneath the trolley.

issues.object: Anaesthesia workstation behind the operating table
issues.description: The workstation is dominated by a plain vertical slab, two black rectangular display areas, simplified flowmeter bars and a cylinder with blunt hanging hoses. The visible control and breathing-system area lacks the structural detail expected of the focal medical device.
issues.why: The large blank surfaces and primitive controls read as a blockout rather than a detailed clinical workstation. The hoses have little connector or mounting definition.
issues.correct_result: A coherent workstation with supported monitor housing, readable control modules, identifiable flowmeters, detailed hose connections and a mechanically plausible breathing-system assembly.
issues.root_cause: The asset appears to use simplified placeholder geometry and incomplete device-specific surface detail.
issues.proposed_fix: Rework the front assembly in Blender using one consistent workstation reference. Add monitor supports, control recesses, dial geometry, flowmeter housings, connector collars and hose attachment points. Add small bevels and weighted normals to the cabinet and worktop. Use an atlas for labels and control markings, retaining simplified geometry only on hidden faces.
issues.expected: The workstation will read as functional medical equipment rather than stacked basic shapes.
issues.verification_needed: Provide a front three-quarter close-up at the c2_anaesthesia distance, with the controls, monitor mounting and hose terminations clearly visible.

history.evidence: c2_anaesthesia clearly shows the slab-like workstation backing, two blank dark displays, simplified vertical controls and blunt-ended hoses around a plain cylinder.
c1_table: the workstation retains a broad plain backing, black display rectangles, rudimentary flow controls and a cylindrical component with blunt-ended hoses.

issues.object: Operating-table padding, side rails and pedestal
issues.description: The operating table has thick, uniformly block-like cushions, simple rail bars and a largely featureless pedestal. Visible padding divisions are not supported by comparably detailed section joints or articulation hardware.
issues.why: The table reads as padded blocks on a basic plinth. Its main silhouette is recognizable, but the visible construction lacks the mechanical detail required at this viewing distance.
issues.correct_result: A proportionally convincing segmented operating table with shaped upholstery, thin support decks, articulated section joints, rail mounts and a defined lifting pedestal.
issues.root_cause: The model has been reduced beyond the detail level needed for a central close-view asset.
issues.proposed_fix: Refine the cushion profiles and rounded edge transitions in Blender. Model the visible section pivots, deck separations, side-rail brackets and pedestal collars from a consistent reference. Preserve clean shading with bevels and weighted normals, and add restrained vinyl grain and seam detail through textures.
issues.expected: The table will have a believable mechanical hierarchy and less toy-like padding.
issues.verification_needed: Repeat c1_table and add a side-level close-up showing cushion profiles, rail brackets and section joints.

history.evidence: c1_table shows thick rectangular cushions, a simple perimeter frame and rails, and a largely featureless pedestal without convincing section articulation.

issues.object: Both surgical-light heads and visible suspension assembly
issues.description: The surgical-light faces are flat textured white discs punctuated by black dots, surrounded by thick simple rims. The suspension and head housings have minimal joint and mounting detail.
issues.why: The optical faces do not read as lenses or reflector modules, and the thick primitive housings are especially conspicuous in this close-up.
issues.correct_result: Recognizable surgical-light optical assemblies with lens depth, a clean protective face, shaped housings, defined adjustment handles and credible articulated joints.
issues.root_cause: Generic disc geometry and a basic face texture are standing in for the optical assembly and mechanical construction.
issues.proposed_fix: Rebuild the light faces with shallow recessed lens modules or a reference-correct lens array. Add housing bevels, pivot collars and mounting joints; refine the handle shape. Separate housing, lens, handle and emissive materials, using a shared normal atlas for small optical detail where necessary.
issues.expected: The lights will read as clinical optical equipment rather than decorative illuminated discs.
issues.verification_needed: Repeat c3_light at the same distance, showing lens depth, housing edge quality and articulated mounting detail.

issues.object: Mayo stand, utility trolley, table rails and exposed equipment metal
issues.description: The exposed metal surfaces mostly read as dull grey-green painted material. The Mayo tray, trolley frame and table rails show little metallic highlight or reflection response.
issues.why: Different equipment surfaces collapse into the same matte appearance instead of separating stainless steel, painted housings, plastic and upholstery.
issues.correct_result: Controlled stainless-steel reflections on trays and rails, softer painted finishes on housings, and distinct rubber and upholstery responses.
issues.root_cause: Metallic and smoothness values may be inappropriate or uniform, compounded by weak reflection-probe coverage.
issues.proposed_fix: Assign separate URP Lit materials by surface type. For exposed stainless steel, use a neutral metallic base with calibrated moderate smoothness and subtle fine brushed detail. Keep painted components nonmetallic. Bake a room reflection probe and verify its bounds and renderer assignment before tuning highlights.
issues.expected: Equipment will gain clear material identity and readable edge highlights without becoming mirror-like.
issues.verification_needed: Provide matching c1_table and c4_cupboard_mayo views showing differentiated tray, frame, wheel and cushion responses.

issues.object: Suspended ceiling tile surfaces
issues.description: The ceiling tiles read as smooth grey panels with broad cloudy variation and grid lines rather than textured acoustic tiles.
issues.why: The ceiling occupies a large visible area and lacks the fine surface texture that establishes the approved benchmark's ceiling finish.
issues.correct_result: Neutral acoustic panels with consistent fine porous detail, restrained roughness variation and crisp grid boundaries.
issues.root_cause: The tile material lacks an appropriately scaled acoustic normal map, or the current texture is too low-frequency.
issues.proposed_fix: Use a seamless acoustic-tile albedo and normal set at real-world scale. Keep albedo variation subtle, place most pore detail in the normal and roughness channels, and check mip filtering on Quest. Preserve the existing grid without baking heavy dark lines into the tile surface.
issues.expected: The ceiling will match the benchmark's surface richness without becoming dirty or visually noisy.
issues.verification_needed: Repeat c3_light with the ceiling in sharp focus, showing fine acoustic texture at both near and distant tiles.

issues.root_cause: Secondary construction details and edge treatment were omitted during asset simplification.
issues.proposed_fix: Add small bevels to the casing and doors, establish consistent door gaps, and model visible hinges or a reference-correct concealed-hinge construction. Refine handle attachment points and give the door finish subtle roughness variation rather than heavy wear.

issues.verification_needed: Provide a three-quarter close-up showing door edges, handle attachments and the cabinet side.

issues.object: Male lab coat neckline, collar edges, front opening, and lower hem
issues.description: The male neckline has jagged pale projections and exposed-looking dark patches around the shoulders and neck. The lower front opening also reads as a narrow irregular slit, with abrupt notches in the hem rather than a clean garment overlap.
issues.why: The collar looks torn or intersecting rather than deliberately constructed. These defects are conspicuous at normal conversation distance and break the appearance of an intact clinical garment.
issues.correct_result: A continuous collar and lapel assembly with clean edges, a controlled front overlap, and an intentional, finished hem.
issues.root_cause: Poorly connected garment boundaries, intersecting collar surfaces, or deformation weights pulling thin neckline geometry apart.
issues.proposed_fix: In Blender, inspect the neckline and front opening with backface and wireframe views. Remove overlapping or stray faces, rebuild the collar and lapel boundaries, add restrained edge thickness, and correct normals. Repaint neck and clavicle weights so the coat remains separate from the neck and undershirt in this pose. Rebuild the front overlap and hem instead of leaving an irregular slit.
issues.expected: The coat will read as an intact tailored garment instead of a damaged shell.
issues.verification_needed: Provide front, side, and rear-neck close-ups of the male in the final pose, plus a full-length view showing the repaired front opening and hem.

issues.object: Both lab coats, especially shoulder caps, bent elbows, and female upper back
issues.description: The coats have balloon-like shoulders and sleeves. The male shoulder width is exaggerated relative to his neck and head, and the female bent sleeve forms a large smooth bulb with little indication of an elbow or fabric compression.
issues.why: The silhouettes resemble padded suits rather than lightweight woven lab coats. Cloth volume is not responding convincingly to the underlying anatomy or bent-arm poses.
issues.correct_result: Modest garment ease over believable shoulders, narrower sleeves, and localized compression and tension folds at elbows, armpits, and waist.
issues.root_cause: Excessive garment offset combined with broad skin weights and insufficient pose-specific deformation.
issues.proposed_fix: Refit the coats to the body meshes in Blender, reduce shoulder and upper-arm volume, and establish shoulder and sleeve seams. Reweight shoulder and elbow regions and add corrective shape keys for these static poses. Sculpt a small number of broad compression folds rather than uniformly inflating the sleeves.
issues.expected: Both figures will have credible anatomy beneath their clothing and more natural conversational silhouettes.
issues.verification_needed: Show matched front and side full-body renders of both staff, with additional shoulder and bent-elbow close-ups.

history.evidence: s4_female_front and s2_male_side show broad rounded male shoulder caps and inflated sleeves. The female bent sleeve in s4_female_front forms a large smooth elbow bulb with little compression-fold structure.

issues.object: Both coat surfaces and exposed scrub trousers
issues.description: The coats are largely featureless gray-white surfaces, with little visible fabric structure or finished construction. The trousers similarly read as smooth color fields. Coat pockets, closures, and clear seam construction are not readable.
issues.why: The clothing reads as a single molded surface rather than layered woven garments and falls below the benchmark's detailed PBR treatment.
issues.correct_result: Matte woven fabric with restrained surface variation, readable major seams, finished cuffs, and plausible coat pockets and closures.
issues.root_cause: Minimal garment texture maps and insufficient modeled or baked construction detail.
issues.proposed_fix: Create a shared Quest-appropriate clothing atlas with subtle fabric normal detail, low-contrast albedo variation, and controlled high roughness. Bake shoulder, sleeve, cuff, pocket, and front-placket seams from a detailed garment source. Model the pocket openings and major overlapping edges where they affect silhouette, and add a restrained button or concealed-closure treatment.
issues.expected: The coats and scrubs will read as distinct fabrics with believable construction rather than smooth shells.
issues.verification_needed: Provide chest, cuff, and trouser close-ups under the final neutral lighting, at both conversation distance and a closer material-inspection distance.

issues.object: Both raised hands and their contact with the blue boards
issues.description: The fingers are spread across or alongside the board faces without a convincing supporting grip. The female side view particularly shows an open, splayed hand beside the board rather than fingers wrapping its edge.
issues.why: The props appear attached to the pose rather than held by the hands. Finger placement does not communicate how the board's weight is supported.
issues.correct_result: A deliberate grip with the thumb opposing the fingers, visible edge contact, and a wrist aligned naturally with the forearm.
issues.root_cause: Generic hand poses reused without fitting the fingers to the prop dimensions.
issues.proposed_fix: Finalize the prop dimensions first, then pose every finger joint in Blender around a specific edge or lower corner. Set thumb opposition, lightly curl the fingertips, and position the palm against the prop without penetration. Save these as dedicated static grip poses and verify the exported wrist and finger transforms in Unity.
issues.expected: The boards will appear physically supported and the staff gestures will look intentional.
issues.verification_needed: Provide palm-side and back-of-hand close-ups for each grip, including an oblique view that reveals the thumb and board edge simultaneously.

issues.object: Blue handheld boards
issues.description: The handheld props read as thick, plain blue slabs with small white rectangular marks. No readable paper stack, clip mechanism, binding, or other construction explains whether they are clipboards or folders.
issues.why: Their large uninterrupted faces and slab-like edges make them look like placeholders, especially against the hands and torso.
issues.correct_result: Recognizable clinical clipboards or folders with consistent real-world dimensions and the minimum construction detail needed to identify their function.
issues.root_cause: Placeholder box geometry and flat colors retained in the final staff setup.
issues.proposed_fix: Choose a specific prop type. For a clipboard, model a thin beveled backing, a low-poly metal clip, and a shallow paper stack with a restrained form texture. For a folder, model separate covers, a spine, and visible paper edges. Scale against an A4 or letter-size reference and refit the grips.
issues.expected: The props will read as practical hospital documentation equipment rather than generic blocks.
issues.verification_needed: Show each prop from the front and edge while held, with the clip or spine and paper construction clearly visible.

issues.object: Male face, especially eyes and mouth
issues.description: The male eyes are extremely wide, with conspicuous exposed whites and a fixed stare. The slightly open mouth exposes a bright, continuous-looking tooth strip, producing a tense expression rather than a neutral staff interaction.
issues.why: The eyelids do not frame the eyes naturally, and the combined eye and mouth pose gives the character a startled, mannequin-like appearance.

issues.proposed_fix: Adjust the eyelid mesh or facial blendshapes to cover the upper iris naturally and reduce excessive lower-eye exposure. Aim both eyes at a shared conversational target and verify convergence. Close or relax the mouth and check lip thickness and tooth visibility from front and three-quarter views.
issues.expected: The face will appear attentive and human rather than startled or rigid.
issues.verification_needed: Provide front and three-quarter head close-ups of the final expression, plus a two-character view confirming the gaze relationship.

issues.object: Character lighting, shoe-to-floor contact, and garment self-shadowing

Check URP main-light shadow distance, cascade coverage, and bias at the staff location; reduce excessive bias without introducing acne. Rebalance ambient and probe contribution against the neutral key light. For the static staging, verify actual sole contact with the floor and use a restrained Quest-compatible contact-shadow solution if required.

issues.root_cause: Insufficient baked occlusion, missing shadow casting, or inadequate light-probe and shadow configuration.
issues.proposed_fix: Bake static architectural and furniture shadows with adequate lightmap texel density and padding. Enable appropriate shadow casting for characters and wheels, tune shadow bias to retain contact, and provide probes for dynamic occupants using a Quest-budgeted lighting setup.
issues.expected: People and props become grounded without simply darkening the entire corridor.
issues.verification_needed: Low-angle screenshots of shoes, bench feet, and wheelchair wheels with final target-platform lighting enabled.

issues.object: End windows and adjacent corridor floor
issues.description: Large bright windows do not produce a discernible sunlight patch or window-frame shadows on the interior surfaces.
issues.why: The exterior brightness is disconnected from the interior illumination, and the requested window-driven sunlight is not demonstrated.
issues.correct_result: Neutral daylight entering from a consistent exterior direction, with visible frame shadows and softer indirect fill.
issues.root_cause: A bright exterior background without corresponding directional lighting or shadow participation.
issues.proposed_fix: Set a neutral directional sun at an angle that reaches the corridor through the glazing. Ensure opaque mullions cast shadows and glazing does not block the light as an opaque surface. Bake the static sun contribution where practical for Quest.
issues.expected: Clearer daylight direction and credible connection between windows and interior lighting.
issues.verification_needed: A wide window-facing view showing the sunlit floor or wall area, frame-shadow pattern, and the associated window.

issues.object: Ceiling light panels and surrounding acoustic tiles
issues.description: The panels are featureless white and several generate intense localized halos on the surrounding ceiling, emphasizing a blotchy tile appearance.
issues.why: The ceiling reads as unevenly illuminated rather than as acoustic panels under broad, controlled hospital lighting.
issues.correct_result: Bright diffusers with restrained glow and smooth, broad illumination across textured acoustic tiles.
issues.root_cause: Excessive emission or bloom combined with overly concentrated fixture lighting and uneven baked illumination.
issues.proposed_fix: Reduce fixture emission and bloom, rebalance exposure, and replace concentrated ceiling-facing light contributions with controlled baked downward illumination. Review tile albedo and normal strength separately from the lightmap.
issues.expected: A calmer ceiling with retained tile texture and fewer artificial white hotspots.
issues.verification_needed: An upward corridor screenshot using final exposure, plus a close-up containing a diffuser and several surrounding tiles.

issues.object: Perforated waiting benches and tubular supports
issues.description: Perforations are visible, but the stainless surfaces read as uniformly dull gray with fine sparkling noise rather than coherent metal reflections.
issues.why: The seat panels, rounded armrests, and supports lack the distinct reflection response expected from perforated stainless steel.
issues.correct_result: Stable perforation detail, controlled brushed-metal highlights, and readable changes in reflection across curved tubes and flat panels.
issues.root_cause: Incorrect metallic/smoothness values, missing reflection probes, and undersampled perforation or normal detail.
issues.proposed_fix: Use a calibrated URP metallic material with neutral metal base color and moderate roughness, add baked reflection-probe coverage, and correct tube normals. Use mipmapped, coverage-preserving perforation textures or a suitable LOD rather than subpixel detail that sparkles on Quest.
issues.expected: Benches read as stainless furniture without noisy highlights or a painted-plastic appearance.
issues.verification_needed: Bench close-ups from two viewing angles and a short headset-resolution camera movement demonstrating stable perforations.

issues.object: Exterior glazing and buildings beyond
issues.description: The window view is dominated by repetitive blue-white facade bands with little atmospheric separation, while the glazing provides almost no readable reflection or surface response.
issues.why: The exterior resembles a close backdrop and the glass reads mostly as an empty opening.
issues.correct_result: Restrained glazing reflections over a legible exterior with believable distance and varied facade response.
issues.root_cause: Overly uniform exterior facade materials and glazing without suitable reflection-probe or Fresnel response.
issues.proposed_fix: Separate facade frame and glass material responses, reduce repetitive high-contrast window variation, and introduce restrained distance haze. Give interior glazing subtle neutral tint and Fresnel-weighted probe reflections using a Quest-compatible shader; retain clear exterior visibility.
issues.expected: Windows gain believable depth and glass presence without becoming mirror-like.
issues.verification_needed: Oblique and frontal window screenshots showing both exterior depth and subtle interior reflections.

issues.object: Wall-mounted picture frames
issues.description: Numerous frames contain uniform gray inserts rather than visible artwork or information.
issues.why: Repeated blank inserts look like unfinished assets, especially beside the populated noticeboard.
issues.correct_result: A limited, consistent set of finished hospital artwork or information panels, with unnecessary frames removed.
issues.root_cause: Placeholder textures or unassigned picture materials.
issues.proposed_fix: Assign correctly UV-mapped, appropriately sized artwork textures to the existing inserts, using an atlas where useful for Quest. Remove surplus frames rather than adding more decoration.
issues.expected: The existing wall decoration appears complete without increasing clutter.
issues.verification_needed: Eye-level screenshots of both corridor walls with frame contents readable at the intended viewing distance.

issues.object: Circular wall object high on the left wall
issues.description: The circular silver-rimmed object has a blank gray face, unlike the completed clocks visible elsewhere.
issues.why: Its presentation reads as an unfinished clock or an unexplained fixture.
issues.correct_result: A complete clock face with hands and markings if this is a clock, or recognizable detailing for its actual function.
issues.root_cause: Missing face material or omitted clock components.
issues.proposed_fix: Verify the asset's intended role. Restore its clock-face texture and hands, or replace it with the correct identifiable fixture model.
issues.expected: The wall object becomes legible rather than appearing to be a placeholder.
issues.verification_needed: A close-up of the circular object showing its completed functional detail.

issues.object: Tall plant to the right of the reception display
issues.description: The foliage has conspicuous layered, jagged card silhouettes and broad flat gray-green patches.
issues.why: The leaf clusters read as intersecting cutout sheets rather than a volumetric plant.
issues.correct_result: A coherent plant silhouette with varied leaf orientation and stable, clean alpha edges.
issues.root_cause: Coarse foliage cards, unsuitable alpha mipmaps, or inconsistent card normals.
issues.proposed_fix: Reorient and reduce obvious planar clusters in Blender, correct foliage normals, and tune alpha clipping and coverage-preserving mipmaps in Unity. Validate the selected LOD at the reception viewing distance.
issues.expected: Less visibly synthetic foliage at the focal end of the corridor.
issues.verification_needed: Reception plant close-ups from the front and side at final render resolution.

issues.object: Overall illumination, particularly operating-table padding, workstation front and staff
issues.description: The room remains uniformly subdued, with bright ceiling diffusers but insufficient readable illumination on equipment and people.
issues.why: The luminous fixtures do not produce a convincing well-lit clinical working environment. Dark equipment faces and compressed midtones suppress both shape and material separation.
issues.correct_result: Neutral clinical illumination with readable workstation controls, teal padding and staff faces, retaining soft shadows and controlled ceiling highlights.
issues.root_cause: Emissive panel materials may not be supported by sufficient baked illumination, and indirect lighting or exposure may be too low.
issues.proposed_fix: Check the URP lighting setup rather than increasing emission alone. Use neutral-white baked area lighting aligned to the ceiling diffusers, confirm lightmap contribution and UVs, and place light probes around staff and movable equipment. Rebalance light intensity and fixed exposure against the PatientBay reference without adding a warm tint.
issues.expected: Equipment fronts and staff become legible while ceiling panels retain detail and the room gains natural tonal depth.
issues.verification_needed: Repeat all three views at the same exposure, including a c1_table close-up showing readable workstation controls and cushion shading.

issues.object: Floor beneath trolley wheels, Mayo stand and operating-table base
issues.description: Equipment shadows include concentrated blurry patches beneath trolley centres while individual caster and frame contact remains weak.
issues.why: The shadow shapes do not adequately describe the equipment above them, making the bases appear weakly anchored.
issues.correct_result: Tight contact at wheel-floor interfaces with softer, shape-corresponding shadows extending from frames and bases.
issues.root_cause: Overbroad ambient occlusion, low-resolution baked shadows, excessive shadow bias or insufficient local shadow contribution.
issues.proposed_fix: Inspect lighting with AO disabled to separate occlusion from cast shadows. Correct floor and caster contact in Blender, improve local lightmap density for static equipment, and tune supported URP shadow bias and resolution for movable objects. Reduce broad AO blobs rather than using AO as a substitute for cast shadows.
issues.expected: Wheels and bases appear grounded without isolated dark stains beneath otherwise weakly shadowed frames.
issues.verification_needed: Low oblique close-ups of trolley casters, Mayo feet and table base, plus the matching c1_table overview.

issues.object: Anaesthesia workstation behind the operating table
issues.description: The workstation remains a plain slab with blank screens, elementary flow-control shapes and a simple cylinder with short blunt-ended hoses.
issues.why: The primary clinical equipment lacks the layered controls, connections and breathing-system construction needed to read as a credible anaesthesia machine.
issues.correct_result: A coherent workstation with identifiable monitor housings, control modules, gas-flow components and a connected breathing system.
issues.root_cause: Proxy-level geometry and screen materials have been retained in the final scene.
issues.proposed_fix: Rebuild the visible front in Blender using a consistent workstation reference. Add recessed control panels, shaped knobs, readable flow tubes, connector ports, hose couplings and a supported breathing-system assembly. Replace black rectangles with plausible powered or explicitly inactive screen surfaces, including bezel depth and glass response. Use shared trim sheets and efficient hose meshes for Quest.
issues.expected: The workstation reads as functional medical equipment rather than a generic cabinet with attached primitives.
issues.verification_needed: Front and three-quarter workstation close-ups showing control geometry, screen treatment and complete visible hose connections.

issues.object: Operating-table cushions, side rails, underframe and pedestal
issues.description: The table uses thick rectangular cushion blocks over a simple slab and rail structure, with little visible articulation hardware and a plain box-like pedestal.
issues.why: Cushion divisions imply independent sections, but the supporting structure does not explain how those sections attach or articulate.
issues.correct_result: A sectioned surgical table with plausible cushion profiles, rail clamps, joints and a mechanically credible lifting pedestal.
issues.root_cause: The model was assembled from basic blocks without a reference-led structural pass.
issues.proposed_fix: Refine cushion thickness and rounded edge profiles, add restrained upholstery seams, and separate the support into matching articulated sections. Model visible hinge axes, rail spacers and accessory clamps. Add pedestal cover breaks and a credible lift-column transition; use bevels and weighted normals on hard surfaces.
issues.expected: The table gains believable scale, construction and section articulation without unnecessary small-part density.
issues.verification_needed: Three-quarter side close-up showing cushion edges, section joints, rail mounting and pedestal transitions.

issues.object: Surgical-light heads and ceiling suspension
issues.description: The surgical lights retain flat ring-pattern faces, thick simple rims and minimally defined suspension joints.
issues.why: The visible faces lack optical depth, and the arms do not convincingly describe the mechanical mounting and adjustment system.
issues.correct_result: Recognizable surgical-light heads with recessed optical elements, shaped housings, central handles and articulated mounting joints.
issues.root_cause: Flat face textures and primitive housings are standing in for modeled light assemblies.
issues.proposed_fix: Model shallow recessed lens or reflector groups, a clear central handle mount and a shaped rear shell. Refine rim silhouettes and add joint collars and pivot housings to the arms. Use geometry for silhouette-critical parts and a shared normal/roughness atlas for smaller details.
issues.expected: The lights read as manufactured surgical fixtures instead of patterned discs on simple bars.
issues.verification_needed: Upward close-up of both light faces and a side view of their suspension joints.

issues.object: Mayo tray and stand, trolley frame and operating-table rails
issues.description: Exposed metal surfaces share a dull grey-green appearance with little highlight or reflection variation.
issues.why: Stainless equipment is difficult to distinguish from painted structural parts, weakening the intended PBR material hierarchy.
issues.correct_result: Controlled stainless-steel reflections, readable edge highlights and clearly differentiated painted and polymer components.
issues.root_cause: Uniform rough materials, missing metallic values or inadequate environment reflection capture may be contributing.
issues.proposed_fix: Separate stainless, painted metal and rubber material assignments. In URP Lit, use metallic values near one for bare stainless and tune smoothness to a satin finish rather than mirror chrome. Add subtle directional roughness detail, small edge bevels and an appropriately baked reflection probe covering the equipment zone.
issues.expected: Trays and rails gain restrained metallic highlights while rubber wheels and painted parts remain visually distinct.
issues.verification_needed: Matched c1_table view and close-ups of the Mayo tray rim and trolley uprights showing highlight variation without blown-out reflections.

issues.object: Suspended ceiling tile surfaces
issues.description: The ceiling reads as smooth panels with cloudy large-scale variation rather than acoustic tile.
issues.why: The missing fine surface structure breaks the ceiling material match with the approved hospital benchmark.
issues.correct_result: Subtly textured acoustic tiles with consistent scale, restrained colour variation and clean grid separation.
issues.root_cause: The material relies on low-frequency colour variation without suitable fine normal or roughness detail.
issues.proposed_fix: Use a correctly scaled acoustic-tile albedo, subtle normal and roughness set. Reduce broad cloudy contrast, verify UV scale per tile, and test mip levels and compression at the target Quest viewing distance so the texture neither disappears nor shimmers.
issues.expected: The ceiling reads as a manufactured acoustic system rather than flat grey panels.
issues.verification_needed: Repeat ot1_from_door plus an upward close-up under neutral lighting showing fine texture and grid edges.

issues.object: Instrument group on the Mayo tray
issues.description: The instruments remain thin, similar grey strips with poorly differentiated handles and working ends.
issues.why: Their silhouettes do not communicate a credible set of surgical instruments at this viewing distance.
issues.correct_result: A small, recognizable instrument set with distinct handle types, thicknesses, pivots and tips.
issues.root_cause: Over-simplified instrument meshes and nearly identical materials erase identifying features.
issues.proposed_fix: Replace the strips with reference-based low-poly scissors, forceps and clamps as appropriate. Preserve ring handles, jaws, pivots and thickness in geometry, with small bevels and a shared stainless material. Space them so their distinguishing silhouettes remain visible.
issues.expected: The tray reads as prepared clinical equipment rather than a row of generic bars.
issues.verification_needed: A tray close-up at intended interaction distance showing distinct grips, pivots and working ends.

issues.object: Rear double-door cupboard
issues.description: The cupboard has handles and vents but retains sharp box edges and minimally defined doors and hardware.
issues.why: The flat door treatment lacks the construction depth expected alongside detailed hospital equipment.
issues.correct_result: A manufactured cupboard with modest edge radii, door returns, consistent gaps and readable hardware.
issues.root_cause: Basic cabinet geometry has not received a finishing pass.
issues.proposed_fix: Add small outer bevels, shallow door returns and consistent reveal gaps in Blender. Define hinge or concealed-hinge mounting breaks appropriate to the chosen cabinet reference, and refine handle attachments.
issues.expected: The cabinet gains believable construction without adding clutter.
issues.verification_needed: Front three-quarter cupboard close-up showing door gaps, edge highlights and handle mounts.

issues.object: Both staff lab coats, especially shoulders, sleeves and torso
issues.description: The coats have inflated, smoothly rounded shoulder and sleeve volumes with little readable collar, front closure, cuff or fabric construction.
issues.why: The garments read as continuous molded shells rather than layered clinical clothing, particularly on the taller staff member.
issues.correct_result: Coats with plausible shoulder fit, defined garment openings and restrained folds that respond to the posed arms.
issues.root_cause: Over-smoothed clothing meshes, limited garment detail and insufficient pose-specific deformation may be contributing.
issues.proposed_fix: Refine shoulder and sleeve volumes in Blender against the underlying body, define lapels or collar, front overlap, cuffs and hem thickness, and add restrained seam and pocket detail. Check skin weights in the displayed clipboard poses and add corrective shapes where shoulders or elbows balloon.
issues.expected: Staff clothing reads as fabric with believable fit rather than inflated smooth geometry.
issues.verification_needed: Front and side close-ups of both staff in these same poses, clearly showing shoulder fit, collar, cuffs and coat closure.

issues.object: Rectangular wall frames and circular wall-mounted fixtures
issues.description: Repeated rectangular frames contain blank grey fields, and the circular wall fixtures show no readable functional face.
issues.why: These repeated blank surfaces look like unfinished placeholders rather than resolved hospital fixtures.
issues.correct_result: Each fixture has a clear purpose and finished surface treatment; unnecessary placeholders are absent.
issues.root_cause: Content textures or functional face details may be unassigned, or placeholder props remain in the room.
issues.proposed_fix: Confirm the intended function of each object. Assign restrained, legible clinical content to required frames; add the appropriate dial, grille or lens detail to circular fixtures. Remove objects that have no functional role rather than adding decorative filler.
issues.expected: Walls appear deliberately finished and functional instead of populated with empty asset shells.
issues.verification_needed: A wall-facing screenshot showing readable frame contents and identifiable circular fixtures at normal room viewing distance.
